checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is reported as [running/confirm] alongside the other arms, and the checklist lists it among '5 running' arms.
findings.problem: Its live_n=3 after the same elapsed period in which control and placebo reached live_n=13, and its screen_n=496 is under a third of control's 1550. An arm accumulating at roughly a quarter of the control arrival rate cannot reach the planned confirm n=600 on the same timeline, yet nothing in the arena display or the checklist flags this. It is reported as a peer of the full-rate arms when it is not one.

findings.claim: 'arms_running' is green with detail '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x'.
findings.problem: The check counts registered arms, not arms that have produced scored live evidence. Every listed arm has live_n between 3 and 13 against a planned confirm n=600, so the green mark establishes registration only. It does not establish that the arena is generating usable confirm-tier evidence, which is what the checkbox title implies.

findings.claim: Each arm carries screen_dWR (e.g. sl-5pct screen_dWR=5.29pp, hold-12h 3.23pp, tp-7pct -3.42pp) as its headline delta versus control.
findings.problem: These deltas are computed on screen_n of roughly 1550, which comes from the backfill tier (4764 backfill events vs 50 live). The checklist itself states 'Only live-tape evidence can promote'. Presenting a backfill-derived dWR as the primary per-arm number in the arena invites exactly the promotion-on-backfill error the check exists to prevent, especially since no live dWR is reported at all.

findings.claim: entry-8pct screen_dWR=0.0pp, vol-4x screen_dWR=0.0pp, placebo screen_dWR=0.0pp.
findings.problem: entry-8pct and vol-4x have screen_wr of 51.613 and 51.27 against control's 49.935, so their true win-rate deltas are not zero. Reporting 0.0pp for arms whose populations were subset by their own filter conflates 'not comparable on a paired basis' with 'no difference', and it makes them visually indistinguishable from the placebo, whose 0.0pp is a genuine inertness result (b=0 c=0).

findings.claim: 'paired_population' is green: '4814 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them'.
findings.problem: Seeing an event is not scoring one. entry-8pct has screen_n=496 and vol-4x has screen_n=866 out of 1550 for control, because their filters decline most detections — declined=47 and declined=40 respectively versus 33 for control. The green check therefore establishes shared detection input, not the identical scored population its title claims, and the arm-vs-arm deltas above rest on non-overlapping subsets.

findings.claim: 'kernel_agreement' is green at 195/200 (97.5%) with an entry-granularity gap of 0.59pp declared as not affecting arm-vs-arm comparisons.
findings.problem: The stated justification is that all arms share the kernel, but two running arms are entry-side filters — entry-8pct on pump_pct and vol-4x on vol_threshold — whose accept/decline decision depends on the measured pump size. A systematic +0.59pp overstatement of pump size shifts which detections cross an 8.0% threshold, so the bias is not common-mode for threshold arms the way it is for sl-5pct or tp-7pct.
